label: Syn3A
plain: A bacterium with a designed, minimised genome: 452 protein-coding genes kept from Mycoplasma mycoides, in a cell about 400 nm across with one membrane and no wall. It grows on its own in a rich medium, and its genome is smaller than that of any natural cell that does.

modelled.text: A note of 14 November 2026 proposes this organism as the first whole-cell validation organism for Cells. Support for it in the engine is being worked on (the user, 14 November 2026; decision D171 gives it an agent under the lead). Nothing of it is in the engine yet: the project's record holds an evidence audit and a proposal, in which no engine model ran.

levels.label: One cell
levels.note: Drawn as a sphere 0.4 µm across with 500 ribosomes: round numbers for the smaller of the two cells that were measured. The larger one was about 0.5 µm across.

no_further_levels: A single-celled organism: each cell lives on its own, so there is no tissue, organ or body.

facts.label: Shape and size
facts.value: a sphere about 400 nm across; two cells measured in electron tomograms were 403 nm and 495 nm across

facts.label: Envelope
facts.value: one membrane; no cell wall and no periplasm

facts.label: Inside
facts.value: no nucleus: in electron tomograms the ribosomes are spread through the whole cell, with the chromosome among them

facts.label: Genes
facts.value: 493, of which 452 code for proteins; the genome record lists 455 protein products, 3 of them added for genetic manipulation

facts.label: Ribosomes
facts.value: about 500 in a small cell: 503 or 684 counted in the cell 403 nm across, by two ways of counting, and 820 or 1,095 in the one 495 nm across

facts.label: Proteins
facts.value: about 77,000 molecules in an average cell, an estimate from proteomics; 427 of the 452 kinds were detected, and the added marker tetM

facts.label: Energy
facts.value: ATP from sugar breakdown alone; no oxidative phosphorylation

facts.label: Food
facts.value: glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and cholesterol, taken up from a rich medium that is not fully defined

facts.label: Division
facts.value: ftsZ and sepF are among seven genes needed together for regular shape and division

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: a genome designed and synthesised from that of Mycoplasma mycoides subspecies capri, strain GM12, and cut down to a minimum

cap.membrane.note: Its one membrane holds the cell's ion and proton gradients. In mycoplasmas the ATP synthase typically runs backwards and pumps protons out; that was measured in related species, not in this strain.

cap.channels.why: No ion channel was found among its 455 proteins: none carries the signature of a channel family in Cells' catalogue, or of the bacterial channels for potassium, chloride, magnesium, water or membrane stretch, which the same search does find in other mollicutes. Its ions cross the membrane through transporters and pumps.

cap.pumps.note: Not the pumps of animal cells: it has no sodium-potassium pump. By its annotation, its ATP-driven ion movers are the ATP synthase, two P-type ATPases named as magnesium transporters, and a potassium uptake system.

cap.junctions.why: It lives as single cells and has no gap junctions: none of its proteins carries the signature of connexins or innexins.

cap.extracellular.note: Here it is the growth medium around the single cell, which the cell depends on. By the 2019 reconstruction of its metabolism it takes up glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and cholesterol from a rich medium.

cap.water.note: It has no cell wall: nothing but the membrane bounds its volume.

cap.calcium.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum: it is a bacterium with a single membrane and no internal compartments, and none of its proteins carries the signature of the store's calcium pump or of its release channels.

cap.energy.note: All of its ATP comes from breaking down sugar in the cytoplasm; it has no proteins for oxidative phosphorylation.

cap.mitochondria.why: It is a bacterium and has no mitochondria. Its ATP synthase sits in the cell membrane.

cap.circuits.note: At the chromosome, which lies in the cytoplasm: there is no nucleus. The minimised genome kept few regulatory proteins.

cap.grn.why: It forms no tissue, so there is nothing for gene networks to be coupled across. Gene expression within the one cell belongs with regulatory circuits.

cap.trafficking.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum and no Golgi. By its annotation, new membrane proteins are put straight into the cell membrane by the Sec translocon and the YidC insertase.

cap.assembly.note: Its assemblies are its ribosomes, RNA polymerase and the ATP synthase. The designed protein cage that Cells models is not one of its proteins.

cap.machines.note: About 500 ribosomes, with RNA polymerase, the ATP synthase and the protein translocon. None of its proteins carries the proteasome's signature; its annotation lists the proteases FtsH and Lon.

cap.secretion.note: By the 2019 reconstruction of its metabolism it releases the end products of sugar breakdown, lactate and acetate, into the medium and takes nutrients up. Signalling between its cells was not looked for.

cap.repair.note: The place would be its bare membrane. No source read for this file describes a membrane injury or its resealing in this organism.

cap.division.note: It grows and divides as a single cell. Seven genes that the smaller strain JCVI-syn3.0 lacks, the division genes ftsZ and sepF among them, are needed together for its regular shape and division.

cap.replacement.why: It forms no tissue, so there is no neighbour for a new cell to replace.

cap.mechanics.why: It forms no sheet: its cells share no edges to pull on.

cap.sheet.why: It lives as single cells and forms no sheet of coupled cells.
